nodes.name: Mechanical Polishing Preparation and Electropolishing
nodes.procedure: The specimen was processed using a fine-cutting machine supplied with cooling water to minimize thermal deformation. The processed specimen was mounted with epoxy resin over an exposed area of 4 cm² and then mechanically polished step by step up to emery paper #220. Once polished, the specimen was ultrasonically washed with acetone and distilled water, and electropolishing was performed after completely drying it in a dryer for 24 h. The electropolishing process was performed for 5 min by applying a current density of 400 mA cm⁻² in an electrolyte in which sulfuric acid and phosphoric acid were mixed at a volume ratio of 2:8 at 75 °C. These are the optimal conditions calculated in the Taguchi robust design.

nodes.name: Cathodic Sputtering
nodes.procedure: A cathodic sputtering process was performed to remove oxides and impurities formed on the surface of the stainless steel before plasma ion nitriding. In the cathodic sputtering process, 300 V were applied for 1 h in a mixed gas environment of 25% nitrogen to 75% hydrogen at a chamber pressure of 300 Pa.

nodes.name: Plasma Ion Nitriding
nodes.procedure: Plasma ion nitriding after the cathodic sputtering process was performed by applying 350 V for 4 h at 450 °C and a chamber atmosphere of 350 Pa with the same mixed gas as the cathodic sputtering process conditions (25% N2 + 75% H2).
